chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) or he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Women are four: Jamia' (the all-encompassing), Mujma' (the gathering), Rabee' (the spring-like), Murba' (the four-fold), Karb (the constraining), Muqmi' (the suppressing), Ghull (the shackle), Qamil (the lousy).'.
And in another hadith: 'And Khurqa' (the torn one), Muqmi' (the suppressing) instead of Karb (the constraining)'.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of women described in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* presents a classical typology of women, categorizing them into four archetypes: the comprehensive and agreeable, the fertile and abundant, the sorrowful and subdued, and the bound and louse-ridden (indicating stubbornness or impurity). The variation in the second narration, substituting 'Khirqa' (ragged/rough) for 'Karb' (sorrow), highlights the nuanced scholarly discussion regarding whether these traits refer to physical appearance, emotional disposition, or marital compatibility, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of spouse selection in Shia tradition.
